utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In light of what you saw in Kravica on the morning of the 14th, did you do anything to engage the civil protection unit?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: The civil protection unit for cleaning up of the terrain and sanitation measures had been mobilised for a long time in Bratunac. Back in 1992 is when it started functioning. However, since there was a need to involve more personnel in that unit, which until then was at the level of a platoon, meaning about 30 people, some other parts of other units of civil protection were added to that unit, such as fire protection unit and labour unit. Therefore, I had no reason to mobilise again those units, to remobilise them. They had already been mobilised. It is just that they were sent to perform that assignment by the municipal civil protection staff, which functioned or operated as needed. Chief of the municipal civilian protection staff was Ljupko Ilic, who also worked with me at the Department of Defence, dealing with civilian protection. Commander of the municipal staff of civilian protection is usually also president of the Executive Board, although it doesn't have to be the case. Therefore, those units of civilian protection which had already been mobilised can be used, if so ordered by the staff of the -- for the civilian protection. And I did not issue orders to those units. My task was to ensure that the units are replenished accordingly and mobilised when needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So you did not have to ask for the civil protection unit to carry out the asanacion [as interpreted] [sic] because that unit was in existence and it was a process by which it would get engaged. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Your question is not clear. Could you please rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I first asked you in light of your position whether you did something with the civil protection to -- with respect to asanacija or the cleaning up of the Kravica warehouse. Concretely, can you tell us yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I personally did not deal with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did the civil protection unit exist at the time for purposes of asanacija?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know whether the civil protection unit of the Bratunac Brigade carried out any asanacija activities?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I think that you used a wrong term. This is not the unit -- civilian protection unit of the Bratunac Brigade, but rather a municipal unit. So this is a municipal civil protection unit, which takes orders from the municipal staff for civilian protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you know whether, do you know whether asanacija was carried out at the Kravica warehouse by the Bratunac municipal civilian protection unit, not civil as it's indicated earlier on the transcript, incidentally, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, incidentally, your authority for mobilisation, where does it finish or where does it -- where are the boundaries? Can you go ...

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: It all ends at the borders of the municipality. So the records are kept based on the residents, both when it comes to residents, people, and when it comes to the place where vehicles were registered. I have no authorities outside of the territory of the municipality, either to mobilise people or equipment or to keep records, outside of the Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Getting back -- I want to clear up one particular detail back to when you drove by the Kravica warehouse, you talked about seeing the dead bodies. Did you see anybody else there, any soldiers, police, anybody?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: There were several groups, quite a lot of troops wearing various uniforms, multi-coloured ones, green ones, camouflage ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of those individuals?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: No. Since the bus, as I've already told you, drove fairly slowly, making it's way and coming across groups of soldiers who were on the road, had I noticed anyone I knew, I would have definitely recognised them. However, I didn't recognise anyone. Despite the fact that I've lived in Bratunac and worked there for so many years and know very many conscripts, hundreds and hundreds of them, perhaps even a thousand, those who went through the Bratunac Brigade. And I probably would have recognised some of them; however, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Another matter, as you indicated, that on the 12th you had gone to Potocari. Would you please tell us how it is that you went to Potocari, how long you stayed there, what was the purpose?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes. I went to Potocari I think at around noon, most likely immediately after the meeting at the command, which General Mladic asked me to attend. I wished to see, together with the president of the Executive Board, Mr. Srbislav Davidovic, nicknamed Buco, whether there were really 20.000 people there, as Mr. Mladic had said. So I went to see what was up there. I went in my private car with the president of the Executive Board, Buco. I found up there Mr. Ljubisav Simic, president of the municipality, who was taking bottles of juice from a truck and distributing it to the people there. It was on the 12th in the middle of the summer, and it was high noon. So it was very warm. People were exhausted, there were elderly there, women, children. There were two, I believe, water tanks. I don't think we had more than two water tanks which were at the disposal of those people. In my view, Mr. Mladic was right when he said that he needed transportation for 20.000 people. Perhaps there were even a few thousand more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you -- could you please describe to us what General Mladic was doing when you saw him.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: It is true that I saw General Mladic at a distance of perhaps some 10 metres. He was talking to individuals, telling them: Don't be afraid. There will be no problems. We will help you here. You can state what you want. If you wish to stay here, just say so. Those who wish to leave Potocari should say so and say where they want to go to. Transportation will be provided. There are trucks here, buses are coming, too. So you should just state your mind. Those who remained in the forests obviously do not wish to surrender; they want to continue fighting. And they will see fighting. Those are the words that I heard him say. I was near him. I stayed no more than 30 minutes there, and then I went back to my office. Because I couldn't be absent for a long time, and I also had to prepare the sending off of the young conscripts. I had to prepare the documentation for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, Mr. Tesic, did you believe General Mladic when he was speaking to those people in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Not for a moment did I believe that anything bad would happen to those people, especially after they received aid and assistance from the president of the municipality and some other authorities who did what they could to alleviate their suffering and to resolve that humanitarian catastrophe. I believed that General Mladic truly wanted to transport these people to where they wanted to go, therefore I didn't doubt his words.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I just have a couple of questions left. During this period, this critical period, the 12th, the 13th, the 14th, 15th, 16th, did you see Mr. Blagojevic or get any requests from him with respect to any activities, be it for mobilisation of trucks and buses or mobilisation for earth-digging equipment?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I don't remember having seen Colonel Blagojevic at all, nor did he -- nor did the brigade send in any special requests.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, where is your office located?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: My office is located in Bratunac in the centre of town, in the old municipality building, on the first floor, the last door to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it from 1995, 1996, 1997, 1998, 1999, 2000, 2001, 2002, 2003, 2004 your office hasn't changed, it's been in the same place?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: My office, the office of the head of the military department, as we always used to refer to it and have been doing for the last 40 years, is in the same place. And before me, several of my predecessors worked in that same office, too, and I continued to work there, too, throughout my term of office. And I assume the person who takes over from me will continue to work in that same office, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. I have no further questions. Thank you very much. You will be asked some questions by Mr. Stojanovic or his colleague and of course the Prosecutor and the Judges. I would ask you to be as complete and forthright as you have been with me. Thank you again, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's time for a break. We'll resume at quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, I heard that you have two questions to ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I hope you could be as concise as possible, because you have taken enough time already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As always, Your Honour. As always.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I could show the gentleman what has come into exhibit as P687. And if we could put the English version on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, if you could look at that document, please. Earlier I asked you whether you -- I had shown you this document yesterday. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you recall looking at this document?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you had indicated that this document reflected that it was -- it had a date or an appointment date of 11 July 1995. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the lower left-hand corner, the 11th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if you could look at paragraph number 4.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I have had a look at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, having looked at number 4 and now that your memory is somewhat refreshed, would it not appear from reading this document that President Karadzic -- Miroslav Deronjic, the commissioner of Srebrenica is being entrusted with certain duties and responsibilities with respect to the civilians from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So let me ask you this. Having looked at this now and having heard the conversation on the afternoon of the 12th in the SDS office, a conversation between President Karadzic and Miroslav Deronjic, can you assist us whether President Karadzic was making -- was passing on any particular instructions to Mr. Deronjic with respect to the citizens?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: This decision by the president of the republic, Mr. Radovan Karadzic, is very decisive in speaking about all the tasks and assignments he is issuing to Miroslav Deronjic by appointing him civilian commissioner for the Serbian municipality of Srebrenica. And he is requesting that all the functions of the municipal authority organs be established and to ensure that they function efficiently, and that in cooperation with the Ministry of the Interior, they should establish the functioning of the public security station in order to provide safety to citizens and their property and to protect businesses and prevent crimes. And in point 4 it says that: "The commissioner," that is to say Mr. Miroslav Deronjic, "shall ensure that all civilian and military organs treat all citizens who participated in combat against the Army of Republika Srpska should be treated as prisoners of war, and to ensure that the civilian population can freely choose where they wish to live or move to." "The decisions by the civilian commissioner shall be binding upon all civilian authority organs in the Serbian municipality of Srebrenica." "The commissioner may appoint his associates." And: "This decision shall enter into force on the day of its adoption," that is to say on the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Blagojevic. THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I should just like to say the following: A moment ago, that is to say in the previous session, the civil defence or civilian protection of the Bratunac Brigade was mentioned. This seemed to me to be ill-intentioned. So could that matter be cleared up, please. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I believe this matter has been cleared up by the direct examination. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Tesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the Court's indulgence, I would like to ask several questions to clear up the dilemma.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, in the direct examination you spoke about the structures and units of civilian protection. Am I right in saying that the units of civilian protection are not led by the municipal board of civilian protection at all?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And that the municipal staffs of the civilian protection within the frameworks of the self protection are under the control of the regional staffs of civilian protection. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The regional staffs and thereby the municipal staffs are under the command of the republican staff of civilian protection. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that within the system of social self protection and according to the provisions thereof, which relate to the functioning and organisation of civilian protection, civilian protection is not under the command of the army at all but has its own system of leadership and command in conformity with the law. Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To all intents and purposes, the unit for asanacija or sanitisation as a specialised unit of protection would come under this system of control and command within the frameworks of the system of civilian protection. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tesic. My second set of questions refers to what you said in the examination-in-chief and the instructions you handed in, as far as I was able to understand. And in article 2 it speaks of the replenishment and mobilisation of wartime units with military conscripts. Am I right in saying that in the same way the wartime units are replenished with materiel resources, that is to say they are replenished with the technical resources and materiel equipment that is needed to carry on a war?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would that mean then that it is true and correct to say that if a war unit needs a certain machinery, for example, as a resource, then a request for replenishment of that kind is made by the corps command to the secretary of the Ministry of Defence and the secretary of the Ministry of Defence issues an order which binds the departments of the ministry to supply the machines necessary to carry out this replenishment?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would I also be right in saying that it is precisely in keeping with the instructions governing mobilisation and requisitioning that we cannot have a situation in which the head of an engineers unit, for example, comes directly to the department of the Ministry of Defence and asks for certain machines or other resources to be requisitioned, mobilised, without following the procedure provided for by the instructions and guidelines and without knowledge of the commander -- assistant commander?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: What I don't know what happened in this specific case, but rules and regulations stand as they stand. And this is how things should be done, through a request and through the secretariat. The replenishment plans are given the okay. But during the war, a lot of other things had to be mobilised and requisitioned to make things over simple. For example, at times what was necessary was the mobilisation of a tractor, a cultivator, agricultural machinery, generally speaking, like saws and so on, and the department would see to that pursuant to the request made by the brigade. I personally can say -- or rather, I don't know what it was like in the Zvornik Brigade, but the Bratunac Brigade, for example, as far as I know, was not replenished with construction machinery. The 1st Light Infantry Brigade had no need of machinery of this kind, construction machinery. And if it did need this machinery from time to time in order to carry out some construction work or build paths through a forest, for example, then the brigade would ask the department to have it provided with this machinery for a few days. And then we would do this through mobilisation and requisitioning. Now, please be more specific and I'll be happy to answer an additional question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's precisely what we wanted to hear. So in a system it had to go through the corps, through the secretariat, and then an order would be issued to the defence department. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: With your permission, I would like to clarify another issue that came up in examination-in-chief. You said that on that day, on the 14th, you went with recruits or the young troops as we call them to Zvornik, where you had to turn them over so that they can be sent on to their military posts?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember at what time you arrived in Zvornik on that day and to whom and where did you hand over these young recruits?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you that with precision. Assuming that I left at 8.00, then I arrived in Zvornik at 10.00. If I left at 10.00, then I arrived in Zvornik at 12.00. So I couldn't tell you exactly. However, the place where we went in Zvornik was a gathering point where people, not only from Bratunac but also from other municipalities covered by the Zvornik secretariat, meaning in that territory, came. This is where all the young troops came. And then they were assigned to various military posts. I couldn't tell you to which military posts those young recruits were sent, but this is something that can be verified in our records. And from there, they boarded buses and I guess one group went to Jahorina and I guess another one went to Bijeljina. I don't know exactly. I assume this is how it was. At any rate, I handed them over to a person, to an official, of the Zvornik Secretariat who was in charge and who dealt with all the escorts, all those people who escorted these young troops. We exchanged documentation, and this is a very well-developed system which is followed to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Following this -- or rather, this handing over, was it done at the command of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I can't recall. I know that occasionally we went to the building of the Standard company, but I can't remember whether we did it on to day. I know that sometimes the troops gathered by the bridge. Are you from Zvornik yourself? I don't know how to explain that, but it was in the centre, in the open area near the bus station. This is where it was done before; however, on that day I can't recall where I turned those soldiers on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you be able to tell me whether it was in the morning or in the afternoon of the 14th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you well, you personally do not remember whom did you turn these young soldiers over to?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: No, I don't. If these soldiers went to a number of military posts, then they had a number of escorts accompanying them. Because each bus went to a separate military post, and there was an escort on each bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So it is possible that on that occasion, that year, it was also done at the Standard building, as was done previously?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot speculate. I've told you that I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Issa, any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I do have some questions. Perhaps I could just get the podium from my friend.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Tesic.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, I'd just like to go back to the beginning of your examination-in-chief. I understand you said that on the 11th of July you met -- you went to Pribicevac with Mr. Eskic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. It was not on the 11th of July. It was on the 10th.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. So it was on the 10th of July, you went with Mr. Eskic to Pribicevac. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And can you tell us, sir, what exactly is the position of Mr. Eskic.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: He was in charge of personnel affairs in the Bratunac Brigade, and he was a major. Later on, he became lieutenant colonel -- perhaps even at that time he was already lieutenant colonel, but I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. And the members of the Worker Battalion that you handed over in Pribicevac, were they members of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: When the Workers' Battalion is mobilised, it is put under the command of the unit to which it is being handed over, which is to say the Workers' Battalion was put under the command of the Bratunac Brigade as soon as I turned over the VOB 14 form. And it stays under their command until it is sent back to their work obligation. These are short-term assignments, the purpose of which is to assist the army for 7, 10, or 15 days, depending on the situation and the needs.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Did you know, sir, when you were in Pribicevac on that day that Commander Blagojevic was there?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You don't recall seeing Commander Blagojevic at Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. You mentioned earlier, sir, that when you deal with mobilisation issues, you normally have records for the mobilisation of conscripts or equipment. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: What do you mean? What kind of records?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Don't you have records of who was mobilised into the army, when it occurs, what equipment is being used by the army? Isn't that what you told us earlier?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: If you mean the mobilisation of the Workers' Battalion on that day, then yes. All military conscripts are recorded in a list. Their names are put on VOB 14 form, and this is certified and turned over to the commander of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. And what about equipment and other materiel that's used by the army, do you have records of those?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: There were receipt forms concerning the call-up papers. So the defence department kept those as evidence that a certain piece of equipment had been requisitioned or mobilised, whereas the brigade or unit -- I don't mean the brigade, I'm sorry. Not the brigade, but the owner from whom a machinery is requisitioned receives a mobilisation call-up paper as well as a receipt that a certain piece of equipment had been requisitioned. In case that machinery should be damaged or something else, the state would have to compensate the owner, at least that's what the law provides.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. I take it there were records of the buses that were requisitioned from Bratunac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Did you review those records before you came here today?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I don't have those records here. I don't have any of those here. However, we knew these facts almost by heart, because we had so very few buses owned by the Vihor company. So we knew them by heart. These were just several old buses, and there was just one new bus which was used for the regular bus line to Belgrade. As I've already said, we requisitioned a bus owned by a private individual, Rodoljub Trisic. It had some problems and was repaired at the workshop of the Vihor company and requisitioned after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Where are the records relating to the buses now, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: If any of the records exist, they could be found in the archives of the department, or perhaps even at the corps command, since Bratunac Brigade ceased to exist quite a long time ago, as did the documents. The form VOB 8, all of these documents were taken out of Bratunac a long time ago. The VOB 8 form listed all individuals who were assigned to the Bratunac Brigade. And similarly, there should also be records for the buses, which were used by the Bratunac Brigade. As for that particular day, as far as Srebrenica and the evacuation of the people from Potocari is concerned, I don't know whether the Vihor company could have given any other buses for those purposes, because their buses were already in the brigade. This is something that can be verified at the Vihor company as to exactly how many buses, with what licence plates, were owned by the company. This is all I can tell you about the buses in the territory of the Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. So the buses that were from the Vihor company were in the Bratunac Brigade. Is that what you've just told us? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Perhaps two buses were, which were constantly used for the needs of the brigade in order to transport soldiers from positions back home and vice versa. If army needed an additional one or two buses, which is all we had, they contacted us, and we would always requisition them for two or three days until they completed that task. And then the buses would go back to the company, because somebody also had to transport workers, students, citizens.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. Now, who were using all these buses that were used to evacuate the Muslim population? Who were using the buses?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: What do you mean who was using the buses?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Was the army using the buses?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. That wasn't within my purview. If somebody contacted the ministry asking that there be a mobilisation, either of people or equipment, then all that I was responsible for is to turn over either people or the equipment to the command that was in charge. I don't know who used them afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, would it be fair to say, sir, the army requested the buses, so they would likely have used them, don't you think?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: We've already discussed this. There was an order issued by the highest organ of the Ministry of Defence concerning mobilisation of buses, which was based, as we have seen through documentation, on the request given by the Main Staff and then sent down to corps and then below, to the secretariats and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. You've told us that, sir, and I understand that. Did you -- did the Bratunac Brigade, to your knowledge, take part in this process, the evacuation process?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I don't know who drove the buses.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know whether or not the Bratunac Brigade provided buses for the evacuation process?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I don't know that either. I don't wish to speculate. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: It wasn't within my scope of authority -- of responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, earlier, sir, we saw the 12 July 1995 order, among other things, ordering the various brigades to provide all available buses. Can you think of any reason why the brigades wouldn't comply with that order?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: It is a well-known fact that an order coming from a superior command has to be upheld, that order listed several brigades from that area requesting them to provide all available buses for evacuation. All those which they had already had.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. So if the assistant rear services commander of the Bratunac Brigade told investigators of the OTP that he provided two buses and there were other buses that were taken from the Vihor transportation company, would you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: If the assistant commander of the Bratunac Brigade said so -- are you referring to Dragoslav Trisic [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes, he had to know. He was assistant commander for logistics. And if there were indeed were two buses, then he would know whether those two buses were given for evacuation or not, because if an additional bus or two from Vihor company were mobilised - and I told you that they didn't have any more than that, other than that new bus that I've told you about - and it was not feasible to cancel that regular bus line to Belgrade because it was a source of cash income for us, if the line did not operate for a day, two or three, then the Vihor company as a transportation company would lose its right to operate that bus line. I personally cannot remember now whether that bus was also requisitioned for transportation of people in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So what you're saying, sir, is that it's possible that other buses were requisitioned or used for the evacuation that you don't know about. Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it calls for speculation. The question in and of itself is self evident. Anything is possible. What is probable?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we would like to hear what the witness is going to tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you answer that question, sir? Let me repeat the question --

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It's possible, sir, given what you've just told us that if other buses were used for the evacuation, you may not know about those buses? Other buses from the brigade, for example, may have been used that you don't know about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now the question has been changed and it's from the brigade. Now, the question suggested that there were more than two buses.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, we've already established that through the previous questions. I think this is a proper follow-up question at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see no problem with this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Would you like me to repeat the question again, sir, or are you able to answer that?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Is it possible, sir, that other buses were used for the evacuation that you may not know about, perhaps other buses from the brigade. Isn't that possible?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Well, there were no -- I don't know how many buses there. If there were some buses with the brigade, then pursuant to an order they had to be used, since there was an order from the Ministry of Defence sent down to us through the secretariat to requisition buses. We requisitioned all the buses that there were and we turned them over to the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Now, sir, when you requisitioned the buses, first of all how did you keep track of the buses that you requisitioned?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Well, there was a call-up document to requisition a piece of equipment. It was a blue form, MOB 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And how many in total did you personally requisition, the buses?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you exactly. I don't have anything to conceal. I'm telling you that there were perhaps three or four buses from Vihor and then one bus which was privately owned. That's all. We had no more.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And how were these buses fueled? Where did the fuel come from?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I was not in charge of fuel.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Who was in charge of fuel?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: There was a gas station within the compound of Vihor. They mostly tanked fuel there, and the logistics base of the brigade also supplied fuel for them. But I don't know about that and I don't wish to go into that. However, frequently they used the gas station at Vihor.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say "the logistics base of the brigade frequently supplied fuel for them," you obviously know something about that. Can you tell us a little bit more about that?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about that. I couldn't even tell you where it was located at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, how do you know that the logistics base of the brigade supplied the fuel? How do you know that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether that's how I phrased it, that it was the logistics base of the brigade. It was probably the logistics base of the corps. Now, whether it was in Vlasenica or someplace else, I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Are you changing your previous answer now, sir, from what you told us just 2 minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: What do you have in mind? What did I say?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm just asking you, sir, if you're changing your answer. Initially you said it was the logistics bay of the brigade, and now you're saying it's the corps. Are you changing your answer?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was the logistics base, which I think belonged to the corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, who provided security for the buses?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: When do you mean? When the people were transported?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Do you mean physical security? What kind of security do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Physical security for the buses.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I didn't hear the translation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably the soldiers. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Did you know the ultimate destination of the buses?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: They didn't tell you where the buses were supposed to go?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, who is "they"? Who is "they"? "They" is a lot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Issa, I believe you already asked this question and the witness has answered. Because the witness said that he does not know the ultimate destination of the buses.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: He just said no, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sorry. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you, sir, ever receive an accounting of the fuel that was used to transport the buses?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So if the assistant rear services commander Trisic, Mr. Trisic, says that the fuel was used, accounting of 52.000 that was consumed over the month of July and it was used for the transportation of the Muslim population, do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If there -- if she can lay a foundation with respect to the fuel. I believe the gentleman indicated that he didn't have any knowledge with regard to the fuel, and now she's asking him to vouch for what Mr. Trisic said. Now, I can vouch that Mr. Trisic will be coming here to testify, who was originally on the Prosecution list but was taken off. She can pose that question to him directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Issa, will you please lay some foundations for that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm just asking him if he's aware of it, Your Honour. Perhaps he can tell us whether or not he's aware of it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know anything about that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Do you know whether the drivers that drove the buses, sir, were they mobilised into the army?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Well, certainly they were mobilised. That is to say especially those buses were mobilised who were in the army all the time. And they had their permanent drivers, their regular drivers, and they had been mobilised in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So they had been mobilised in the Bratunac Brigade, the drivers of the buses? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what the names of the drivers were, the ones who drove the buses. But I assume that they were drivers from the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Going back to the meetings that you attended, sir, the one on 12 July in the morning, do you remember you told us you attended a meeting in the Bratunac Brigade. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: On the 12th in the morning, yes. As I said, the meeting when General Mladic was there. Is that the meeting you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. That's the meeting I'm referring to, sir. You mentioned, sir, that there were approximately 12 to 15 people at that meeting. Can you tell us who those people were.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell you even half their names. I remember and I can certainly say that there was General Mladic at the meeting, the president of the Municipal Assembly, Ljubisav Simic was there; as was the president of the Executive Board, Srbislav Davidovic, nicknamed Buco; then there was the president of the municipal board of the SDS, Miroslav Deronjic; there was myself; and some other officers. But I really can't remember their names and I really couldn't tell you. Perhaps there was someone from the civilian authorities, too, but I really can't remember anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, sir, when you say "there were some other officers," you're referring to members of the army?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And can you tell us where they were from, these other officers, what brigade, what unit. Do you know?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I really don't remember. I don't know. Maybe I didn't even know them, so that's why I couldn't remember. But a lot of time has gone by since then so I really can't remember. But I do know for certain about the ones whose names I gave you. I know they were there for sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Dealing then with the meeting that you said occurred at the SDS on the 12th of July, do you remember that meeting you were talking about earlier?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, but not specifically. Not everything that took place at the meeting. I do remember that a meeting was held in the -- at the SDS premises and I confirm what I said earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. And who was at that meeting, sir? Who else was there?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I can't personally claim who was there by name, the names of the people. But as I say, all the responsible people from the municipality had to be there, including the names I mentioned and also, I assume, members of the board.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Was Ljubisav Simic there?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Well, as I'm here under oath, I can't claim one way or another. I can't swear that I remember him being there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Was Mr. Davidovic there?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I really can't remember. Yes, there were a lot of people there, perhaps 10 or 15, but I daren't say any names if I'm not 100 per cent certain. But there might have been 15 people there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: 15 people at the SDS meeting? There might have been 15 people at that meeting you said?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes. Or let's say 10. Let's make the number lower, 10. I can't be sure. Well, yes, all right. I'm remembering. And I remember there was Ljupko Ilic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Anyone else?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: This is how it was: I could give you some more names of members of the municipal board of the SDS who were members. Now, whether they were actually there at that particular time, at that particular meeting, I don't dare say, because I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And do you know -- do you remember whether there were some members of the army there at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Could there have been members of the army there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, this is a bit way off base. "Could there have been" --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'll withdraw, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now if she wants to say: Was Mr. Blagojevic there, I have no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ms. Issa has promised to move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to deal with your testimony regarding the -- when you attended at Kravica on the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you see any members of the Bratunac Brigade military police when you were there?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I've already said that I did see or I could have recognised -- had I been able to recognise somebody, I would have recognised them and said, because the bus went fairly slowly, perhaps 30 kilometres an hour. But, as I say, I wasn't able to recognise anybody in that situation, although, as I said before, I did know a lot of soldiers from the Bratunac Brigade. But I didn't recognise anybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see Radenko Drkovic there? Do you know who Radenko Drkovic is there?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: It's not Drkovic, it's Djurkovic, if that's who you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, that's who I mean.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: And I can assume why you're asking me that, but no I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know he said he was there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, now we're getting off base. She asked him if he saw him; he said no. The gentleman was here. He testified..

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm entitled to ask some follow-up questions in relation to that. I don't think I have to just stop where Mr. Karnavas is suggesting. This is a cross-examination, after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think the question is improper the way it's being posed because it's trying to suggest that the gentleman is lying.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting that at all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we missed the answer of this witness in the transcript, so I could not make a proper judgement of this dispute. Ms. Issa, will you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Djurkovic said he was there, sir, on the 14th of July. Do you recall seeing him there? Does that help you refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I didn't see him. I don't know. I don't remember, really, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you know if somebody named Krsto Simic?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I don't know that he was there, but I do remember that Krsto Simic was an operator for construction machinery. I think he worked in Sase and that he was a truck driver that carried iron ore, or rather a concentrate of lead and zinc.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you see him at Kravica?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you see any machinery near the bodies?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: No, no. I don't remember having seen that when I passed by. It might have been just a minute. It doesn't take a minute to pass by the Kravica warehouse at Oka. It's just a hundred metres long. So if a bus is moving at 30 kilometres per hour, it just takes him a little while to pass that hundred metres. And I didn't see or recognise anybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. So now you're saying that you didn't pay too much attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. That's not what he said. That is a clear mischaracterisation of the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It's a follow-up question, Your Honour, and I think I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have to listen to Mr. Karnavas first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If you just plainly look at the question. "So now you're saying that you didn't pay too much attention." He indicated that he looked. He indicated the speed. He indicated the time he had available to see, not that he wasn't paying attention. That's a mischaracterisation of his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Issa, I think the witness answered that. "I didn't see or recognise anybody."

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour. I can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, sir, you said early that you saw many bodies at Kravica. Did you report that to anybody, what you had seen?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I was in the bus and I had the task or assignment of taking recruits and to escort them and to hand them over at a particular place. That was my job that day. That was my duty. When I returned in the afternoon, I don't know exactly what time - it might have been 1.00, 2.00, 3.00, I can't remember, when I returned to Bratunac - but it was already known, people knew about that already because many people were surprised when they saw what they saw, especially the members of the work battalion, some of them, or Workers' Battalion, who were coming back from their assignments. And when they came to Kravica, they had something to see and they were taken aback. And then they went to the municipality. They were surprised. They were astounded as to what was going on there. They put their hands up on their heads, and I saw a few days ago from Jovo Nikolic or Jovan Nikolic. I heard how he came to the municipality building, hit his head across his -- his hand across his forehead and said to Ljubo Simic and Miroslav or whoever, he said to the two of them, because they were responsible individuals: What's going on down there? And when I returned, having accomplished my assignment, all this was common knowledge. People knew about it, so all I could do was to confirm that something was going on down there, but people already knew about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So it was common knowledge when you returned back to your knowledge, as far as you were concerned, yourself?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you know what happened to the bodies, sir, what happened to the bodies in Kravica? All those bodies that you saw --

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: You mean with respect to the asanacija, or sanitisation of the terrain and seeing to the bodies being removed, that kind of thing?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I personally don't know about that. I didn't involve myself in that kind of job. That was done by the unit for the asanacion [as interpreted] of the terrain. They had their own commander. And the civilian protection staff, the municipal staff functioned, and the head of the municipal staff was there. And I assumed those people know more about it than I do. I really don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Are you aware that the bodies were dug up at some point after they were initially buried and reburied? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Well, there were rumours to that effect, one, two, or three years ago. There were stories going around town. But otherwise, I personally don't know about that, when it was done, or who did it, or who gave the order, or who took part in it. I really know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you mentioned, sir, that you were on your way to Zvornik when you saw these bodies?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you tell us who were the soldiers that you were taking over there. Who were they?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: You mean their names and surnames?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Those young soldiers, those who were doing their regular -- going to do their regular service. At this point in time, I can't remember a single name.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you recall who you handed them over to in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly who I handed them over to, no. I said I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier, sir, that it can be verified -- names can be verified by your records. Did you try to review those records before you came here?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure that some documents and files and records do exist with respect to the 14th of July, 1995, when these young soldiers were sent there and taken in. I'm sure that records do exist, but just off the bat I can't tell you, except that I do know that I took them there. Now, who those young boys were, their first and last names, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So you're saying that you're sure the records exist, but you didn't try to locate and review them before you came here. Is that right? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't look through those records; I didn't look for them either. But I do know that I went that day, and I remember that well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you mentioned earlier, sir, that you actually went to Potocari because you wanted to see what was going on.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I wanted to see for myself, to see whether it was true.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. How long were you there?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I've already said, half an hour at the outside.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see Muslims getting on to the buses while you were there?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: There weren't many buses, a few buses, and they were all full. And as each of the buses arrived, they would board them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see military age men separated from their families as they were trying to get on the buses?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I didn't see that. It is my impression that of those 20.000 people, if there were that many, I can't say exactly, that 90 per cent or more were women, elderly people. There weren't any military conscripts there. Perhaps there were, but that wasn't my impression, that there were any military-able men there. But some of them were. I don't know. But that was my general impression.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Did you see any Muslims being beaten and kicked onto the buses and abused while they were getting on the buses?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: No. No. No. Mostly people helped those people, helped them board the buses. They helped them. And I've already said that the president Ljubo Simic, I saw him there and I do remember that. I saw him handing out fruit juices and that there was a water cistern, water -- where drinking water had been brought in and water was being distributed because it was hot. And they had even brought in some food. I happen to remember a truck from Ljubovija, from Serbia, from the Azbukovica company, which is a trading company, one of their trucks. And I knew the driver in actual fact, who had driven in a full truck load.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, when you were in Bratunac, were you in your office most of the time or were you in Bratunac on 12 and 13 July? Is that where you were?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I was. I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And how much time did you spend there?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: In the office you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Or in Bratunac on 12 and 13 July.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Well, I've already said. From 7.00 in the morning on the 12th I was at the meeting at the command and in Potocari at around noon. In the late afternoon or early evening, I don't know the time exactly, I was at the meeting at the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So basically, sir, if I can just shorten this, aside from the meetings and spending that half-hour you told us about in Potocari, you were in Bratunac for most of the time on 12 and 13 July. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I say that I was there on the 12th, as I've already said. Now, I can't remember whether it was in the evening hours that I went home or whether I slept in my office because I had a bed there, a bed in my office during those critical days, so I didn't even leave my office. Now as to the 13th, I really can't say for sure, can't remember where I was. Probably I was in my office preparing the documents for the next day because there were a lot of documents to send these recruits the next day, on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you know when you were there in Bratunac, sir, did you know that there were men who were being detained on the buses in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean "detained." I didn't understand the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: There were men that were kept prisoner on the buses in Bratunac, that were parked in Bratunac. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Kept prisoner? Well, this is how it was. What I saw was this: In the evening hours - but I don't know whether it was on the evening of the 12th or the evening of the 13th, I can't say for sure - but I did see in Bratunac, in front of the municipality building in the centre, a large number of buses with men, Muslim men. So from the office I did see that, but I don't know whether that was on the evening of the 12th or the 13th. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Did you know that those Muslim men were also kept in the schools, in the Vuk Karadzic school, and the hangar? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: No. No, I wasn't aware of that. Of course later on there were stories going around, but a lot later. But at that point in time, on that day, that evening, the following day, the day after, I didn't know that. I wasn't aware of that, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you know that the men were taken off the buses in Bratunac and beaten and abused? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were you aware that men were taken off the buses and killed in Bratunac and shot?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you hear any shots in Bratunac during those evenings?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Didn't anyone report this to you, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just for the record, there has been no foundation that anybody should be reporting any of these activities to this particular individual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I don't think I need to lay a foundation for that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, I'm not asking you to lay the foundation. I just want to ask you how long you're going to last for your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I just have a couple more questions and then I'm finished so we don't have to keep this gentleman here over night. I actually didn't realise the time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Did you receive any reports that bodies were found round the buses and the schools in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: There were some individual cases when a corpse would be found. And the unit for asanacion [as interpreted] or sanitisation of the terrain worked on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So you're talking --

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I remember one -- well, since the municipality in the school you mentioned are 50 to 70 metres apart, I remember that there was a body at the entrance, in front of the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And how did you come to know that there was a body in front of the school? Did you see the body?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Because the commander of the unit, Dragan Mirkovic, he reported to Ljupko as the chief of staff. And we were working nearby. So that's how I came to learn about that, I assume.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. You didn't learn about the 50-odd bodies that were in Bratunac? You just learned about that one body?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: No, I did learn about that, and I can't remember that so many bodies were found. I can't remember that there were so many.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And Dragan Mirkovic didn't tell you that there were more bodies?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Mirkovic is his name. Well, he didn't have the duty to report to me at all. He would inform the chief of staff of civilian protection.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And Ljupko didn't tell you either, did he?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that he mentioned that many number of bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And just so that we're reminded of this, sir, who was Ljupko again? You've told us earlier, but can you just tell us again. Is this Ljupko Ilic?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Ljupko Ilic, yes. Yes. He had the duty of chief of staff of the civilian protection and the unit for sanitisation. And it would report orally to the headquarters of the civilian defence protection.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did you know the destination of the buses that carried the men from Bratunac? You mentioned you saw those buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's been asked and answered, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That was a different question, Your Honour. It had nothing to do with the other buses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think earlier on you asked that question, but since you mention that there's a different, you mean the man from Bratunac that night?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you know the destination of those buses, sir, that carried the men from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I don't know that, no. And for a long time afterwards I didn't know and I don't know. And I didn't even know -- no, I don't know where they were taken. I simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I thought they were the people from Potocari who was supposed to be, according to Mladic's words, transported to the territory of the federation towards Kladanj and Tuzla. That's what I thought at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Earlier, sir, you told us you didn't know the ultimate destination of the buses from -- for the people of Potocari?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I didn't say that I did now either. I didn't say I knew now either. What I said was I thought they were being driven off towards Tuzla or Kladanj or wherever they said they wanted to go. Because Mladic on the 12th in Potocari said, and I heard him say that personally, that people should say where they wanted to go and that they would be taken there. So that's what I thought then.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Now, sir, earlier you mentioned that you went to Srebrenica and you saw some ugly things in Srebrenica. Do you remember that? Do you remember telling us that? What are those ugly things?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date, but I do know -- I wouldn't have gone up there at all to see that. There was nothing to see, just ugly things. But I went the insistence and invitation of Rodoljub Djukanovic who at the time was the republican trades inspector, otherwise he was from Bratunac originally and I know him well. And with him there was another man. He was the vice-president - I can't remember his name - the vice premier of the Republika Srpska and some other people like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: We are pressed for time, sir, and I would like you to answer my question. My question is: What are the ugly things you saw in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Well, I meant the fact that the town was in a pitiful state from the aspects of hygiene, it was in a very poor state. Now, imagine this, as soon as you approached Srebrenica, lice and fleas started biting you and you had to scratch. You began scratching yourself. That's what I meant. And all the black buildings. There was very little place for accommodation and a lot of people there. So they had broken down the walls and had made fires and all the smoke had turned all the walls and buildings black.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Yes or no, did you see bodies when you were in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. How many mosques were in Srebrenica when the Republika Srpska took over on 11 July?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to this question. What is the relevance with respect to the mosques? I don't see anything in the indictment with respect to destruction of religious properties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, it goes to the issue of persecutions and genocide. I think if the gentleman can answer the question, I think it could tell us --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, before the question is posed again, the Prosecutor repeatedly over and over again says the attack on Srebrenica was lawful. Nothing in the indictment says that any mosques were targeted and as a result there are [sic] counts in the indictment. They repeatedly tell us that the attacks are lawful and yet now they're trying to go through the back door.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think we're not talking about the attack on Srebrenica at this time, but I could not remember whether the destroying of property, of mosques, was mentioned in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: As I understand it, Your Honour, Mr. Ruez did testify about it but it's not specifically referred to in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's not in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It is my last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If it's not mentioned in the indictment, you should not ask this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just one question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, the records of your office, the records, where are they normally kept?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: On the premises. In the office, there are metal filing cabinets, and that's where the records to be stored are stored. If there is an expiry date, then they are destroyed. That kind of thing. Some documents are kept for 2 years, 5 years, 10 years. Some things lost -- are kept always. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Has -- has anybody come to look for those documents or to look at those documents?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: You mean linked to Srebrenica? Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was it from the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: From the Prosecution, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Who was it that came to look for those documents that have been available over there?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: A state commission turned up from Republika Srpska. And in it were one of the commission members, Smail Cekic was his name, a Bosniak by ethnicity and a lawyer Djordje Stojakovic from Banja Luka. And another from the Ministry of Defence from Banja Luka. His name was Zoran Cvetkovic. They were there for five hours about a month ago, roughly. I can't tell you the exact date. They looked through the documents. The regular post, the confidential post, the strictly confidential post, everything was placed at their disposal so that they could look at it. Before their arrival, I was informed of their imminent arrival by my superior officer, the secretary of the secretariat of Srpsko Sarajevo, Mr. Milomir Krajic [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. If the Prosecution wanted to look at those documents after all these years that have gone by in the same office that you have been occupying all these years right in the middle of Bratunac, would you have made those documents available to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR TESIC
utterances.text: Everything that has to be done has to be done by law. Nothing is hidden. Everything is there. Nothing has been thrown away, disposed of. What there is there is there. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. At this stage are there any documents to tender? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, there are some documents. I have it here. D114, D117, D118, D119, and D120.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any objections? Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Those documents are admitted into the evidence. On your side, Ms. Issa, are there any documents to tender?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we have no documents to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you, Witness, for your coming to The Hague to give your evidence. And when this hearing is adjourned, the usher will show you out of the room. And at this stage, I would like to remind the parties to make the best use of their time at their disposal, because we are about 15 minutes delayed in this sitting. I think the -- especially for the person who is conducting the direct examination. And at the same time, I would like to thank all the people working for us, the security people, the interpreters, as well as the court reporter, for their cooperation. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
